transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh… yeah, I guess it was something at work. I’m a personal care aide, so we have these staff meetings, you know, about safety stuff, and they were talking about fall prevention. And I just got really worked up and kind of… started acting the whole thing out.

Like I was moving chairs around and waving my arms, showing how someone might fall and how to catch them or not catch them, and people kept telling me to sit down. I heard them, but I couldn’t really stop right then. It got embarrassing. I didn’t mean to make a scene.
Has this kind of thing happened to you before?

Yeah… I mean, not exactly like that every time, but I’ve gotten worked up before where I kind of start showing people what I mean instead of just saying it. This one was at the staff meeting, the fall-prevention thing, and I was moving chairs around and waving my arms like I was doing the whole drill right there.

People were saying, “Sit down,” and I heard them, I did, but it was like my body was already in it. I couldn’t quite stop right away. It’s embarrassing, because I’m not trying to be difficult. I just get carried off with it sometimes.
Do you think these episodes have caused problems for you at work or in your relationships with others?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I don’t like saying it like that, but they put me on leave from the senior center after all that, and that’s… that’s my work, you know? I’m used to helping people, getting them up right, making sure they’re okay, and now I’m sitting at home thinking about whether I can even go back safely.

And at home my wife’s been on me— not in a bad way, she’s just reminding me about chores, appointments, stuff I used to keep track of better. I’ll mean to do it, then it slips, and then there’s dishes or laundry or some paper I was supposed to bring somewhere.

I’ve pulled back from church people too. They ask how I’m doing and I don’t know what to say, and then I start feeling like everybody’s watching me, so I just don’t go as much or I leave quick. It’s caused problems, yeah.
Do you ever have thoughts that you think might not be true, but you believe them anyway?

Yeah… I guess that’s kind of the hard part. Like, part of me can say maybe I’m making too much of it, but even when I’m calm, I still feel pretty sure my supervisor and a couple people at work are keeping notes on me.

Not just normal notes, I mean… like watching how I move, what I say, making little comments to test me. Like they’re trying to prove I’m not safe around the seniors. And then I start thinking back to things they said in the hallway, or during meetings, and it all kind of lines up in my head. I don’t know. Maybe that sounds off, but it feels real to me.
Do these thoughts about your supervisor and coworkers keeping notes on you stay with you most of the time?

Yeah… most of the time, I’d say. It kind of sits in the back of my head even when I’m not upset. Like I can be making coffee or looking for my keys, and then I’ll remember something my supervisor said, or some little comment from somebody at work, and it feels like… see, that was part of it.

Not like regular paperwork, I mean like they’re keeping track of me, testing me, trying to catch me doing something wrong so they can say I’m not safe with the seniors. And I know people say jobs keep notes, that’s normal, but this feels more personal than that. It stays with me, yeah.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

Yeah, sometimes. I know what I’m trying to say, but it’s like my mind is already three steps ahead of my mouth.

I’ll start talking about work, like the senior center, and then I’m thinking about church, and then my wife asking me about something at home, and then some idea I had for a workshop or a better way to do things, and by the time I try to explain it, I lost the first part. Then people look at me like, “What are you talking about?” and I get frustrated because it made sense in my head a second ago.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking to people?

Yeah, I do. I’ll be talking and it’s like my mind hops around too fast — I start with my job, then I’m thinking about church, then my wife, then some idea for a workshop or something I wanted to start, and by then I’ve lost the first thing I was trying to say.

It’s frustrating, because it feels connected in my head, but when it comes out, people don’t always follow it.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words?

Yeah… disjointed, that’s a good word for it. I’ll be trying to explain one thing, like something at my job, and then my mind jumps over to church, then to my wife, then I’m thinking about some workshop idea I had, like maybe something that could help people, and by the time I come back around I forgot what I was saying in the first place.

It’s like the thoughts are moving faster than I can get them out, and then I sound mixed up even though it felt connected in my head.
Do you often have trouble sticking to one topic when you're talking to someone?

Yeah, I do. I try to stay on one thing, but my mind jumps quick. Like I’ll start talking about my job, then all of a sudden I’m thinking about church, then my wife, then some idea for a workshop I wanted to do, and it all feels connected to me at the time.

But by the time I’m trying to say it, I already lost the first thought, and then I’m kind of chasing it. So yeah, I have trouble sticking with one topic sometimes.
Do you ever have thoughts that just pop into your head and feel like they're not your own?

I don’t know… not really like that, I don’t think. I mean, thoughts pop in my head all the time, but they feel like mine, just fast or random sometimes.

Like I might be thinking about work and then suddenly remember something at home, or something somebody said, but I wouldn’t say it feels like somebody put it there. Unless… I don’t know exactly what you mean by “not my own.”
Do you find it difficult to organize your thoughts before expressing them to others?

Yeah, it is hard. I’ll try to get it straight in my head before I say it, but then it starts moving too quick. Like I’m thinking about my job, and then somehow I’m on church, then my wife, then an idea for a workshop, and it all feels like it makes sense for a second.

But when I try to explain it out loud, I lose the first thought before I can say it right. Then I’m just kind of talking around it, trying to catch back up.
Do you think your way of thinking has ever led you to do things that didn't make sense to others?

Yeah… I think so. Like, that’s kind of why I’m here.

There was this staff meeting at work, and we were talking about fall prevention, you know, keeping people safe, and I started getting worked up because I could see it in my head. So I stood up and started acting it out with the chairs, like moving them around, waving my arms, showing how somebody could fall and how we should catch it before it happens.

And people were telling me, “Sit down, sit down,” but I couldn’t really stop right then. It made sense to me, like I was demonstrating it, but I know to them it probably looked like I was acting strange.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like all day or anything, but it happens.

Like if I’m by myself in the hallway at work, I’ll hear my name, clear as day, or like one of the residents calling for help. And I’ll stop and go check, because you don’t want to ignore that, you know, that’s part of the job… but then nobody’s there.

It’s happened at home too, like near the laundry room. I’ll think somebody called me, but when I look, there’s no one. It makes me feel kind of uneasy, because it sounds real when it happens.
Do you think the voices you hear are coming from inside your head or from outside?

It feels like it’s from outside, mostly. Like not just a thought in my head. When I’m alone in the hallway at work, I’ll hear my name, or one of the residents calling for help, clear as day, and I turn around like someone’s actually there.

Same thing at home sometimes, near the laundry room. I’ll go check because it sounds real, you know, like it’s coming from the room or down the hall… but then nobody’s there.
Do you often find it hard to make yourself understood when talking to others because your thoughts seem disorganized?

I don’t know… I mean, I don’t always think about it that way. Sometimes I feel like I’m explaining something clear, but then people look at me like they’re waiting for the point, you know?

But I can usually talk to people at work, like with residents or staff, if it’s basic stuff. I might go around the long way getting to what I mean. My girlfriend says I add too much detail sometimes. So… hard to make myself understood? Maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if my thoughts are disorganized exactly.
Do you feel like your thoughts are more disorganized when you're stressed or upset?

Yeah… especially when I’m stressed, it’s like everything starts jumping around in my head. I’ll be trying to answer one thing, and then my mind goes from my job, to church, to my wife, to some idea I had for a workshop or fixing something, and by the time I try to say the first part out loud, I already lost it.

Then I sound like I’m not making sense, but in my head it felt connected for a second. It’s frustrating.
Is your thinking usually disorganized, or does it mostly happen when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Mostly when I’m stressed or upset, I think. I mean, it can happen other times too, but stress makes it worse. My mind starts jumping real fast — like I’ll be thinking about my job, then church, then my wife, then some workshop idea I wanted to do, and it’s all connected for a second in my head.

But then when I try to say it, I lose the first thought before I can get it out right. Then I’m talking and I can tell I’m kind of going around in circles.
Do you believe that people are actually watching you or plotting against you, even when there's no evidence?

Yeah… I mean, I know people say “you don’t have proof,” but it doesn’t feel like nothing to me.

Even when I’m calm, I still feel pretty sure my supervisor and a couple people at work are keeping notes on me. Like they’ll make these little comments, kind of testing me, seeing how I react… like they’re trying to build something to say I’m not safe around the seniors.

And I know that sounds like I’m jumping to conclusions, but when you’re there every day, you notice the way people say things. Like one comment by itself maybe isn’t much, but all of it together… it feels planned.
Do you feel like you're in control of your thoughts and actions when you're hearing voices or feeling like people are watching you?

Not really, no… I mean, I think I’m in control, but then something happens and I kind of get carried away.

Like the thing that really brought me in was this staff meeting. We were talking about safety stuff, and I got worked up about fall prevention with the seniors, because I’ve seen how a chair can be in the wrong place and then everybody acts like it’s nobody’s fault. And I started showing them, like acting out the whole drill right there with the chairs, moving around, waving my arms, showing how someone could fall.

People kept telling me to sit down, and I heard them, but I couldn’t seem to stop. I was trying to make my point, but it got bigger than that. It was embarrassing after.
Do you experience periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that last for days or weeks at a time?

Yeah… I do get like that. Not all the time, but there’ll be stretches where I feel really bright, like fired up, like everything is finally lining up and I can see what needs to happen.

And then if somebody slows me down or starts questioning me, I don’t take it good. I’ll snap harder than I mean to. Like, I’m not trying to be that way, but in the moment it feels like they’re blocking something important. Then later I’m like… why did I come at them like that?

People kept telling me to sit down, and I heard them, but I couldn’t seem to stop. I was trying to make my point, but it got bigger than that. It was embarrassing after.
